name: Carnival Corporation & plc
legalName: Carnival Corporation (NYSE: CCL) and Carnival plc (LSE/NYSE: CCL, via ADS) operating as a single dual-listed company
exchange: NYSE (Carnival Corporation); Carnival plc also historically listed on London Stock Exchange with ADSs on NYSE
description: Carnival Corporation & plc is the world's largest cruise operator by passenger capacity and revenue, operating a nine-brand portfolio spanning mass-market (Carnival Cruise Line, AIDA, Costa), premium (Princess, Holland America Line, P&O Cruises UK) and luxury (Cunard, Seabourn) tiers. It generates revenue from passenger ticket sales (cabin fares) and onboard/other spending (dining, beverage, casino, shore excursions, and increasingly its own private destinations such as Celebration Key and RelaxAway). Uniquely among major cruise operators, Carnival is structured as a dual-listed company combining Carnival Corporation (Panama-incorporated, Miami-headquartered, NYSE-listed) and Carnival plc (UK-incorporated, Southampton-headquartered) under one management team and board. The company reports results across two geographic ticket/onboard segments (North America and Australia; Europe) plus Cruise Support (shared services, port operations, and other costs supporting global operations) and Tour and Other (primarily Holland America Princess Alaska tour and land operations).

employees.note: ~101,000 shipboard (excluding those on leave) and ~16,000 shoreside (13,000 full-time, 3,000 part-time/seasonal)

businessLines.name: North America and Australia
businessLines.description: Ticket and onboard revenue from Carnival's North America and Australia-sourced brands, predominantly Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line and Seabourn.

revenue.note: Derived by summing disclosed passenger ticket revenue ($10.9B, 62% of segment) and onboard/other revenue ($6.7B, 38% of segment); total not independently confirmed as a single disclosed line item

businessLines.revenueNote: Derived by summing disclosed passenger ticket revenue ($10.9B, 62% of segment) and onboard/other revenue ($6.7B, 38% of segment); total not independently confirmed as a single disclosed line item

businessLines.name: Europe
businessLines.description: Ticket and onboard revenue from Carnival's Europe-sourced brands, predominantly AIDA, Costa, P&O Cruises (UK) and Cunard.

revenue.note: Derived by summing disclosed passenger ticket revenue ($6.5B, 77% of segment) and onboard/other revenue ($1.9B, 23% of segment); total not independently confirmed as a single disclosed line item

businessLines.revenueNote: Derived by summing disclosed passenger ticket revenue ($6.5B, 77% of segment) and onboard/other revenue ($1.9B, 23% of segment); total not independently confirmed as a single disclosed line item

businessLines.name: Cruise Support
businessLines.description: Costs and revenue related to port operations, shared global services (procurement, IT, marine operations) and other support functions serving all brands; not a consumer-facing revenue line in the way ticket/onboard revenue is.
businessLines.revenueNote: Specific revenue figure not obtained from sources reviewed; segment exists primarily to allocate shared operating costs

businessLines.name: Tour and Other
businessLines.description: Primarily Holland America Princess Alaska tour and land operations (hotels, motorcoaches, rail dome cars) that package land-based Alaska/Canada touring with cruises.
businessLines.revenueNote: Specific revenue figure not obtained from sources reviewed; historically a small single-digit-percent share of total company revenue
